Join the City of Chattanooga Team Chattanooga , a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (UTC) and Chattanooga State Community College , our city blends a rich industrial history with a tech-forward future—famously powered by the nation’s first community-wide "Gig" fiber-optic network.​ The City of Chattanooga was also recently designated as a "National Park City,” the first of its kind in the United States. Our Organization As a City, we are powered by a dedicated workforce of approximately ​ 2,600 employees committed to excellence in public service and making Chattanooga the best community in the country. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including: Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments. Infrastructure Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management. Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library. Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives. Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead. Why Choose Chattanooga? The City of Chattanooga’s workforce is the heartbeat of our community. We don't just offer jobs; we offer careers with purpose: making Chattanooga the best city in America. We are committed to being the premier employer of choice in Southeast Tennessee by providing: Competitive Compensation: Robust pay scales that reflect our commitment to our staff. Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible. Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. . Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization. ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away. ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast. Water Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River. Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges. In Chattanooga, "work-life balance" means you can finish your shift and be at a trailhead or on the water before the sun sets. A huge thank you to the Chattanooga Times Free Press for helping us highlight and celebrate Goodwill’s mission this month. ⭐️ Learn more at: www.goodwillchatt.org/chattanooga-area-goodwill-opportunity…The number of people served by Chattanooga's three Goodwill Opportunity centers, which provide free job search and career advancement services, has grown by 176% over the past nine months, according to Goodwill officials.

A strong region is built when communities have the resources, partnerships and capacity to move forward together.

Today, we’re proud to share the Southeast Tennessee Development District 2026 Annual Report, reflecting a year of meaningful investment and collaboration across the communities we serve.

This year, SETD helped secure $51.9 million in grant funding for local governments, managed more than $450 million in community projects, connected thousands of older adults and individuals with disabilities with critical resources, and provided 13,433 workforce services to 721 regional employers.

But the story of this year is bigger than any one number.

It can be seen in infrastructure moving from plans to reality, new investments reaching our communities, people gaining skills and pathways to employment, older adults remaining connected and independent, and local leaders working across community lines to address shared priorities.

That is the role SETD is proud to play: bringing people, resources and expertise together to help Southeast Tennessee turn shared goals into progress.

None of this work happens alone. We are grateful to our local governments, board members, funding partners, community organizations and regional partners who continue to trust us and work alongside us.

Building Together for a Thriving Southeast Tennessee.

This year asked us to step up for our neighbors, and together, we did.

From helping families stay housed and fed to supporting students in 10 Community Schools, launching Rooted Together, and growing our Thrift Stores, this year was about creating stability and opening doors to what comes next.

Our new Impact Report shares the stories, milestones, and numbers behind that work, and the people who made it possible.

We are deeply saddened by the passing of Shane Morrow, a dedicated community leader and visionary. Shane gave so much of his time, energy and heart to making Chattanooga a better place. Through his leadership and commitment to others, he touched countless lives and helped make our community stronger.Shane Reynald Morrow, beloved life partner, musician, artist, community builder, helper, connector, and visionary, passed away August 26, 2026 at the age of 57. Born in Bridgeport, Connecticut, Shane was the son of the late Cheryl Morrow Tinsley and Larry Black. He graduated from Central High School in Bridgeport and continued his education at Housatonic Community College, where he completed a two-year program in computer programming. Shane was a musician at heart. Coming from generations of piano players, music was both a gift and a language through which he connected with others. But Shane's passion extended far beyond his own creativity. He believed deeply in the power of the arts to bring people together, preserve culture, create opportunity, and make communities stronger. Shane was, above all, a helper and a connector. He had a remarkable ability to see possibility in people, sometimes before they could see it in themselves. He connected artists to opportunities, people to resources, friends to one another, and ideas to the people who could help make them real. If someone needed help, Shane looked for a way to provide it. If someone had a gift that deserved to be seen, he looked for a stage. If there was a door that needed to be opened, Shane would open it. That spirit was at the heart of Jazzanooga, which Shane co-founded with his life partner, James McKissic. What began in 2011 as a celebration of Jazz Appreciation Month grew into an organization dedicated to celebrating Chattanooga's rich Black musical heritage, expanding access to the arts, and creating opportunities for artists and communities too often overlooked. Shane believed that the arts should belong to everyone. He worked to remove the financial, cultural, and social barriers that could prevent people from experiencing them. Under his leadership, Jazzanooga grew from a festival into a year-round community arts organization, eventually evolving into RISE Chattanooga, Responsive Initiatives for Social Empowerment. Through RISE, Shane's vision grew even broader. Music remained central, but so did entrepreneurship, cultural preservation, professional development for creatives, community empowerment, and creating opportunities for Black and Brown artists, businesses, and neighborhoods. Whether through a concert in a city park, a program for young musicians, support for a creative entrepreneur, or simply introducing two people who needed to know one another, Shane understood that building community was about building relationships. Shane's impact cannot be measured only by the organizations he founded, the programs he created, or the performances he helped bring to Chattanooga. His true legacy lives in people: the artists he encouraged, the young people he inspired, the entrepreneurs he supported, the friendships he nurtured, the introductions he made, the opportunities he created, and the many people he helped simply because helping was part of who he was. Shane was preceded in death by his parents, Cheryl Morrow Tinsley and Larry Black. He leaves behind his partner of nearly thirty years, James McKissic, his baby, Zora McKissic; his aunts and uncles Russel Ray, David Ray, Barney Ray, Mary Ray, Lance Morrow, Brent Morrow, Jason Morrow, Eugenia McCallister; and an extended network of cousins, friends, artists, musicians, colleagues, neighbors, and community members whose lives were enriched by Shane’s friendship, generosity, creativity, and care.  Shane believed that creativity could transcend barriers and that everyone deserved the opportunity to experience the joy, dignity, and connection that the arts can provide. He spent his life putting that belief into practice. The music, relationships, organizations, and community Shane helped build will continue. And in each person he connected to another, each artist he encouraged to step onto a stage, each idea he helped become reality, and each person he stopped to help along the way, a part of Shane remains. His was a life of creativity, service, connection, and love. And the community he spent so much of his life building will carry his spirit forward.  The community is invited to join family and friends of Shane Morrow in a celebration of his life through music and the arts on September 20, 2026, 4:00 pm at the Walker Theater in the Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Auditorium, 399 McCallie Avenue Chattanooga, TN 37402. In lieu of flowers, the family invites you to honor Shane’s memory with a donation to the Sankofa Fund for Civic Engagement. Donations will support youth music programs in Chattanooga, reflecting Shane’s love of music, the arts, and the importance of creating opportunities for young people in our community. To make a donation, please visit: https://cfgc.fcsuite.com/erp/donate Select “Sankofa Fund”, and follow the prompts to complete your gift.
